images.title: Mine lift in metres
images.purpose: Show that a mine lift starting at −90 m and moving −55 m reaches −145 m: levels below ground are negative.
images.composition: One tall vertical mine shaft centred, with the ground line near the top and a downward arrow, wide white margins.
images.exact_structure: One vertical shaft with a grey #6B7280 ground line at 0 near the top. Below it, a teal #0072B2 dot at −90, an amber #E69F00 dot at −145 further down, and a reddish purple #CC79A7 downward arrow between them. No other levels. Exactly 1 ground line, 2 dots, 1 arrow.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
an upward arrow, or the end dot placed above the start dot
images.takeaway: Below ground is negative, and moving down adds a negative.
images.description: A mine shaft with the ground at 0 m, a teal dot at −90 m, a downward arrow labelled −55 m, and an amber dot at −145 m.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the start and end dots and say whether the lift went up or down.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
